ABOUT KEYCARD

At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a staff-level Software Engineer, SDK to own the libraries developers use to put Keycard in front of their agents and MCP servers. For most teams, the SDK is the first Keycard code they touch: a few lines that add OAuth to an MCP server, then token exchange so a tool can call GitHub or Google as the user.

Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Our SDKs come in two kinds. The REST API clients for Python, TypeScript, and Go are generated with Stainless from our OpenAPI spec. The agent SDKs are handwritten: OAuth primitives, MCP server and client auth, agent-to-agent (A2A) delegation (in preview), and integrations for frameworks like FastMCP, LangChain, Temporal, and Cloudflare Workers. The hard design work is on the handwritten side.

Python is the most complete today. TypeScript is in preview and working toward parity, and Go and Ruby are earlier. Keeping four languages consistent, without treating any of them as second-class, is the core of the job. You'll work with founders, product, and the engineers building the services underneath.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - API design. Decide what each package exposes and keep it consistent across languages. An AuthProvider in Python should feel like the one in TypeScript, Go, and Ruby, down to errors and credential types.

 - Safe defaults. The SDK verifies tokens, refreshes them, and handles signing-key outages, so the safe path has to be the easy one. A verifier built without an audience should warn. An expired token should refresh, not force a new sign-in.

 - Track upstream. Our MCP package follows the upstream MCP SDK's major versions, and framework integrations are tested nightly against each upstream's latest release. Ship support for new versions quickly, and decide when an old line moves to security fixes only.

 - Releases. Each package versions and publishes on its own, to PyPI, npm, pkg.go.dev http://pkg.go.dev, and RubyGems. Own semver, changelogs, deprecations, and the CI that bumps and publishes on merge.

 - Generated clients. Own the path from our OpenAPI spec to the Stainless-generated clients. Fix problems in the spec, not in generated code.

 - Developer experience. Quick starts, examples, and docs that take someone from install to a protected MCP server, and a loop that turns developer feedback into API changes.

 - Agents at work. Coding agents already open a good share of our SDK pull requests. Decide what they're trusted to do, and keep tests and review strong enough to catch what they get wrong.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You've shipped libraries or SDKs that other developers depend on, and supported them through breaking changes.

 - You've kept one API consistent across at least two languages. You write idiomatic Python and TypeScript; Go or Ruby is a plus.

 - You know OAuth 2.0 and OIDC at the library level: token verification, refresh, PKCE, and token exchange (RFC 8693).

 - You've managed versioning in the real world: peer dependency ranges, maintenance branches, and deprecations users could plan around.

 - You build with MCP and agent frameworks, and have opinions about what works and what doesn't.

 - Agents in your work. You use coding agents daily and know where their output needs a closer look.


STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - Code generation for multi-language SDKs: Stainless, Speakeasy, Fern, OpenAPI, or protobuf.

 - Plugin or integration ecosystems, like Terraform providers, framework adapters, or editor extensions.

 - Contributions to MCP, the A2A protocol (which we support in preview), or open source agent frameworks.

 - Edge runtimes like Cloudflare Workers, or durable execution like Temporal.


YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Close the biggest gaps between the TypeScript and Python SDKs, toward dropping TypeScript's preview label.

 - Publish a cross-language API guide: names, errors, and credential types, mapped across Python, TypeScript, Go, and Ruby.

 - Take one upstream breaking change, like a new MCP SDK major or framework release, from nightly failure to released support.

 - Agree an SDK roadmap with product and engineering, including where generated clients end and handwritten SDKs begin.


WHO WILL LOVE THIS JOB

 - You care about the first ten lines a developer writes with your library.

 - You'd rather design an API once than explain it four different ways.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Build at the Frontier: Work every day at the frontier of agent-native systems — shipping, inventing, and iterating on technology that hasn’t been built before. You’ll be given huge autonomy, the opportunity to gain mastery, and the chance to work in a team that holds each other accountable to succeed.

 - Truly Agent-Native Culture: At Keycard, we don’t just enable others to adopt agents — we use them ourselves to build. You’ll help shape an organization that embeds AI into its foundation as an enduring competitive advantage.

 - Compensation With Upside: Market-competitive salaries and generous equity packages (4-year vest, 1-year cliff) give you the security to focus on building — and the asymmetric upside of ownership in a company chasing a category-defining mission.

 - Comprehensive Benefits & Recharge: Health, dental, vision, and paramedical coverage for you and your family, plus 4 weeks vacation, 11 statutory holidays, and 1 volunteer day annually. We encourage at least 2 weeks off each year to fully recharge.

 - Tools That Keep You Ahead: A new MacBook Pro, a $500 stipend for peripherals, and the best AI tools available so you can work at the forefront of agent-native workflows.

 - Remote-First Flexibility: We are a remote-first team prioritizing asynchronous collaboration, with hiring focused in North and South America. Work where you’re strongest — we just want the best.

If this sounds interesting to you then we have a range of opportunities for you to explore.
  
  
We're looking for PhD students across multiple research domains to invent, design, and implement state-of-the-art solutions for never-before-solved problems. Your work here won't just stay in a notebook — it ships to production and reaches customers worldwide.

Key job responsibilities
  
  
As an Applied Science Intern, you will own the design and development of end-to-end systems. You'll have the opportunity to write technical white papers, create roadmaps and drive production level projects that will support Amazon Science.
  
  
You will work closely with Amazon scientists and other science interns to develop solutions and deploy them into production. You will have the opportunity to design new algorithms, models, or other technical solutions whilst experiencing Amazon's customer focused culture.
  
  
The ideal intern should have the ability to work with diverse groups of people and cross-functional teams to solve complex business problems.
  
  
A day in the life
  
  
You'll spend your first weeks scoping your project with your mentor, then own the research and implementation end-to-end.
  
  
Your work could involve building computer vision models that power live sports experiences for Prime Video, developing multimodal GenAI solutions for AWS document intelligence, creating agentic AI systems that reason and act autonomously, or advancing recommendation models that transform how customers discover content — depending on the team you're matched with.
  
  
Many interns publish at top-tier conferences or see their work deployed to production before the internship ends. Interns may also be considered for a return offer at the end of their internship, subject to performance evaluation and headcount availability.
  
  
Further benefits of an Amazon Science internship include;
  
  

* All of our internships offer a competitive salary
* Interns are paired with an experienced manager and mentor(s)
* Interns get invited to different intern program or office events
* Interns can build their professional and personal network with other Amazon Scientists

**About The Team**
We're hiring interns for multiple teams in Israel, including but not limited to;
  
  

* Prime Video Sports — Build innovative sports experiences for Prime Video, spanning computer vision, 3D simulation, and personalized content recommendations.
* Personalization — Leverage LLMs, NLP, and recommender systems to match customers with products that align with their passions and shopping preferences.
* Agentic AI — Build next-generation agentic AI systems that automate real-world knowledge work, spanning retrieval-augmented generation, multi-agent workflows, long-term memory and personalization, knowledge-graph construction, and agent evaluation.
* DS3 Textract — Develop multimodal generative AI algorithms that pioneer state-of-the-art document understanding solutions impacting millions of customers.

**Description**
 Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. AWS Database Services provides a broad range of purpose\-built database services for any scale. Whether you need relational, key\-value, document, in\-memory, graph, time series, wide column, or ledger databases, AWS has the right database for your needs. As a member of the AWS Database organization, you'll support the development and management of database services that power millions of active customers and handle trillions of transactions.
   

  

 Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database service that does all this and more. DynamoDB is a key\-value and document database that delivers single\-digit\-millisecond performance at any scale. DynamoDB can store petabytes of customer data and handle peaks of more than 20 million requests per second.
   

  

 As a fast growing service at the core of the AWS Cloud, our business and engineering decisions have widespread impact across AWS, Amazon, and beyond. Many of the world's fastest growing businesses, such as Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin, as well as enterprises, such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One, depend on the scale and performance of DynamoDB to support their mission\-critical workloads.
   

  

 DynamoDB is one of the largest distributed database systems in the world, and we continue to believe it is Day 1 for the DynamoDB business. We are constantly improving and adding new capabilities to DynamoDB, and we are looking for a deeply technical, team\-first software development engineer to push DynamoDB even further.
   

  

 DynamoDB engineers are constantly challenged to think of unique and innovative solutions. The quality bar is high. As an engineer here, you will work on the hardest engineering problems in distributed systems at a massive scale and on multiple dimensions. You will exercise your intellectual curiosity, work with motivated teams of sharp individuals, and get insightful guidance from senior and principal engineers.
   

  

 This is a hands\-on position in which you will own everything from end to end: requirements gathering, designs, design reviews, implementations, code reviews, incremental feature launches, operations, mentoring, and the driving of continuous improvement.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

 Design, build, and operate distributed infrastructure systems that provision, bootstrap, and manage the DynamoDB test cluster fleet. Specifically:
   

  

 Own systems end\-to\-end. Take a problem from design through implementation, deployment, and ongoing operation. No handoffs — you build it, you run it, you improve it based on production data.
   

  

 Deliver independently with minimal guidance. Break down ambiguous problems into executable plans. Your manager sets direction; you figure out the how and drive to completion.
   

  

 Debug complex distributed systems issues. Trace failures across multiple services, accounts, and regions. Identify root causes — not just symptoms — and fix them structurally.
   

  

 Write production\-quality code in Python and Java. Ship weekly. Maintain high standards for testing, monitoring, and operational readiness.
   

  

 Operate the fleet on\-call. Triage tickets, respond to alarms, and use what you learn operationally to drive reliability improvements back into the systems.
   

  

 Collaborate across teams. Engage partner teams to unblock dependencies, review designs, and align on technical approaches. Communicate clearly in writing and in person.
   

  

 Influence technical direction. Propose improvements, write design docs, and participate in architecture decisions. You're expected to have opinions backed by data and advocate for them.
   

  

 Mentor junior engineers and interns. Review code, give constructive feedback, and help others grow.
   

  

 In short: You will be a self\-sufficient engineer who can independently own a major workstream, operate what they build, and make the engineers around them more effective.
   

  

 A day in the life
   

  

 Your morning starts with a message: "My test environment won't come up." By 10am you've traced a deployment failure to a race condition between two services, shipped a fix, and unblocked a team of engineers whose pipeline is green again.
   

  

 By noon, you're designing automation that lets any engineer spin up a fully functional multi\-region DynamoDB test environment with a single command — replacing what used to take a week of manual configuration. You're thinking about cross\-region networking, security boundaries, and making complex infrastructure invisible to its users.
   

  

 After lunch, you're debugging a circular dependency that's been silently generating tickets for months. You find it, fix it, and close an entire class of failures.
   

  

 What makes this role different: You're building the infrastructure that lets every DynamoDB team validate their features before they ship to customers. When you make test environments faster and more reliable, you multiply the velocity of hundreds of engineers.
   

  

 The problems are deeply technical — distributed systems orchestration, fleet management, cross\-account security, credential rotation at scale — but you'll ship code every week and see immediate impact.
   

  

 The team is small (6 engineers), the scope is large, and the ownership is real. You'll design, build, and operate entire systems end\-to\-end. You'll work with Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, CloudFormation, EC2 fleet management, IAM, Python, and Java. You'll use AI coding tools daily.
   

  

 Every major DynamoDB launch validates on infrastructure your team builds. You make that possible.

**About Trace**
Trace is building the data, infrastructure, and research that enable robots to learn from the real world. General-purpose robotics requires a deeper understanding of how robots learn from real-world data. Our research explores how to transform human experiences, including egocentric video, demonstrations, hand-object interactions, and multimodal sensory signals, into transferable representations, actionable knowledge, and generalizable robot behaviors. At our Brooklyn research lab, we combine fundamental research in robot learning, computer vision, and embodied AI with large-scale datasets, machine learning infrastructure, and real-world robotic experimentation. Our goal is to advance the science of robot learning while developing the datasets and learning foundations for increasingly capable, adaptable, and reliable robots.
  
  
**About The Role**
We are looking for highly motivated and technically curious Robotics Engineering Interns to join our team in a hands-on hardware-and-software role, contributing to the development of robotic systems, data infrastructure, and experimental platforms that support cutting-edge research in robot learning and embodied AI. This internship is designed primarily for Master's and undergraduate students, although PhD students are also welcome to apply. We value practical robotics experience, strong engineering fundamentals, problem-solving ability, and a genuine interest in robotics research. Prior research publications are not required.
  
  
As a Robotics Engineering Intern, you will work closely with our research scientists, research interns, and engineers to build and operate robotic platforms, develop reliable data collection and processing pipelines, implement and evaluate learning-based robotic systems, and support experiments that connect human and robot data to downstream policy performance. You will have opportunities to take ownership of well-defined engineering and experimental projects, from hardware and software integration through implementation, testing, evaluation, and documentation. Depending on your background and interests, you may also contribute to research experiments, algorithm development, and technical publications. Our goal is to provide meaningful hands-on experience at the intersection of robotics engineering and robot learning research, while giving students opportunities to develop practical skills, deepen their research understanding, and contribute to advances in physical AI.
  
  
**Projects you may work on**
Depending on your experience and interests, your projects may involve one or more of the following areas:
  
  

* Robotic Hardware and System Integration
* Multimodal Data Collection and Infrastructure
* Data Processing, Calibration, and Quality Evaluation
* Human Demonstration and Robot Learning Systems
* Robot Policy Implementation and Evaluation
* Simulation and Experimental Validation

We welcome students with diverse technical backgrounds. You do not need prior experience in every area, and projects will be matched to your skills, interests, and available opportunities.
  
  
**What You’ll Learn And Build**

* Build and integrate robotic systems, working with robot arms, dexterous hands, sensors, cameras, and associated software and hardware interfaces.
* Develop and maintain robotics software and data pipelines for data acquisition, synchronization, processing, storage, visualization, and experimental evaluation.

You'll own features end to end, from piping raw event data into our warehouse to shipping polished, AI-driven user-facing products.
  
  
If you love writing SQL as much as you love writing React, and you're excited by the idea of turning messy behavioral and marketing data into tools people actually use, this is for you.
  
  
**What You'll Do**
You'll build and ship full stack applications in React and Next.js deployed on Vercel, backed by Snowflake and supporting data infrastructure. On any given week you might be architecting a new customer-facing dashboard, writing complex SQL across rich CX and marketing data streams, building ETL pipelines that land clean data in Snowflake, standing up reverse ETL flows that push modeled data back into operational systems, or wiring LLM capabilities into product surfaces so that non-technical teammates can get answers from data conversationally. Dashboarding work in Omni is also part of the mix, both building dashboards directly and building web experiences that embed or extend them.
  
  
**What We're Looking For**

* Strong full stack experience with React, Next.js, and SQL. You can move fluidly between frontend components, API routes, and warehouse queries.
* Comfort deploying and operating on Vercel.
* Hands-on experience with Snowflake (or a comparable cloud warehouse), including schema design, performance tuning, and writing non-trivial analytical SQL.
* Experience building ETL pipelines to ingest data from SaaS sources, event streams, and APIs into a warehouse.
* Experience with reverse ETL patterns to sync warehouse data back out to marketing, CX, or operational tools.
* Ability to design and build dashboards and data visualizations, ideally in Omni (or tools like Looker, Hex, Mode).
* A track record of shipping production web applications, not just prototypes.

****Nice to Haves****

* Experience integrating LLMs or agentic AI into production apps (OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, RAG, tool use, embeddings, vector search).
* Prior work on AI-powered internal tools, conversational analytics, or natural language to SQL interfaces.
* Familiarity with modern data stack tooling like dbt and Fivetran.
* Experience working with CX platforms such as Kustomer, Five9, and Salesforce.
* Experience with marketing platforms such as Klaviyo.

**JOB SUMMARY:**
As a Data Scientist for Choice's Revenue Management Agentic Systems and Pricing Analytics team, you will use AI, data science, and revenue management expertise to solve pricing, forecasting, and commercial performance questions at the brand, market, and hotel/property level. You will design, build, test, and deploy agentic AI frameworks that support pricing analysis, demand forecasting, elasticity measurement, dynamic pricing recommendations, and causal inference analytics. You will partner with Revenue Management, Pricing, Analytics, Product, and Technology teams to convert business questions into scalable models, agents, and decision-support tools that improve key KPIs such as RevPAR, RPI, ADR, occupancy, and competitive price position. This individual-contributor role will develop predictive models, evaluate pricing and promotional strategies, and help modernize RM workflows through the responsible use of AI platforms such as Claude, Copilot, and OpenAI. The role requires hands-on experience with model development, validation, agent rollouts, and production-ready analytics that improve pricing strategy and revenue outcomes.
  
  
**RESPONSIBILITIES:**
**Agentic AI Systems, Model Operations and Data Engineering**

* Design, develop, test, and roll out agentic AI frameworks that support Revenue Management and pricing workflows, including agents for pricing diagnostics, demand signals, competitive insights, and recommendation support.
* Build and maintain data pipelines, feature stores, model-ready datasets, and analytical tools using SQL, Python, and approved enterprise data sources.
* Implement responsible AI patterns for agent orchestration, evaluation, monitoring, prompt/version control, guardrails, token throttling, and hierarchical model routing.
* Use AI platforms such as Claude, CoWork, Copilot, and OpenAI to prototype, deploy, and scale agents in partnership with Technology, Product, and Analytics teams.
* Create system health and model performance KPIs for AI-enabled RM solutions, including adoption, latency, accuracy, quality, cost efficiency, and business impact.

**Predictive Forecasting, Elasticity, Dynamic Pricing and Causal Analytics**

* Develop and validate predictive demand forecasting models for short-term and long-term revenue management planning at the brand, market, and hotel/property level.
* Estimate price elasticity, demand sensitivity, booking pace, segmentation behavior, and competitive response to inform pricing strategy and rate recommendations.
* Apply causal inference, experiment design, A/B testing, uplift measurement, and statistical validation to evaluate pricing, promotional, and RM initiatives.
* Analyze historical and forward-looking data to identify patterns, trends, and revenue opportunities that improve RevPAR, RPI, ADR, and occupancy.
* Translate model outputs into clear recommendations, visualizations, and executive-ready insights for Revenue Management and Pricing stakeholders.

**Revenue Management Strategy, Competitive Analysis and Stakeholder Delivery**

* Perform competitive analysis using internal and external market signals to guide pricing strategy at the brand, market, and hotel/property level.
* Identify opportunities to improve RevPAR, RPI, ADR, occupancy, price position, and revenue capture through scalable pricing analytics and RM decision support.
* Partner with Revenue Management, Pricing, Brand, Product, Operations, and Technology teams to prioritize use cases based on business value, feasibility, and adoption impact.
* Develop business cases, analytical readouts, implementation plans, and stakeholder materials that support commercial decisions and RM transformation initiatives.
* Manage intake of analytical and AI-agent requests, define success metrics, and support deployment, training, change management, and post-launch measurement.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**
**Employment Experience**

* 2+ years of professional experience using structured and unstructured data to perform statistical analysis, build predictive models, and provide business insights.
* Hands-on experience developing predictive demand forecasting, price elasticity, dynamic pricing, causal inference, experimentation, and machine learning models.
* Demonstrated experience building, deploying, or operationalizing AI agents or agentic workflows using Claude, CoWork, Copilot, OpenAI, or comparable enterprise AI platforms.
* Experience with token throttling, hierarchical model routing, model evaluation, prompt/version management, guardrails, monitoring, and responsible AI practices for production or business-facing agents.

**Technical Skills**

* High proficiency in Python, SQL, and/or R, with experience using supervised and unsupervised learning methods, statistical modeling, feature engineering, validation, and testing.
* Experience with ML frameworks or libraries such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, Scikit-Learn, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or Semantic Kernel is a plus.
* Professional experience creating data visualizations and executive-ready analytics using Tableau, Power BI, Excel, Matplotlib, or Seaborn.
* Proficient in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and business intelligence tools; familiarity with Microsoft Copilot and M365 productivity workflows preferred.

**Additional Skills & Competencies**

* Strong strategic and critical thinking skills, with the ability to draw conclusions from data and translate analytical findings into RM and pricing recommendations.
* Ability to decompose Revenue Management and Pricing questions into analytical, AI-agent, and model-development use cases with clear success metrics.
* Strong communication, storytelling, teamwork, collaboration, organization, and stakeholder management skills.
* Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust and work across departments and disciplines to design practical solutions.
* Knowledge of pricing, revenue management, hotel revenue strategy, RevPAR, RPI, ADR, occupancy, segmentation, and distribution principles is strongly preferred.

**Education Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Engineering, Business Analytics, Information Systems, or a related quantitative field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
* A master’s degree in a related quantitative field is preferred.

**Description**
As a Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) on the Custom Model and Optimization team, you embed directly with strategic customers to build, optimize, and run custom generative AI models in production alongside their engineering teams. You own complete model workstreams end-to-end from defining the evaluation bar and preparing data, through training and inference optimization, to production deployment.
  
  
FDE IIs on this team works at the intersection of models and systems. They customize state-of-the-art open-weight and foundation models for new domains, languages, and modalities; migrate and optimize training and inference workloads on AWS Trainium and operate those models as production services. They are autonomous contributors who take on projects where the business goal is clear, but the path is not. They make design trade-offs with appropriate guidance, limit short-term workarounds, coach others on producing high-quality code, and train new team members.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
Embed within customer ML and engineering teams: Understand the customer's business, data, model stack, and operational constraints. Translate ambiguous goals into a measurable evaluation bar and a technical plan for your workstream such as model selection, customization approach, and serving architecture. Requires up to 25% travel.
  
  
Customize and post-train models. Adapt open-weight and foundation models to customer domains through continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning (including RLHF, RL with verifiable rewards, and multi-turn agentic RL). Build the data pipelines, synthetic data generation, and evaluation harnesses that prove a customized model out performs the baseline on the customer's own quality, latency, and cost bar. Apply these techniques to high-value patterns such as coding agents, domain foundation models, and multi-adapter serving.
  
  
Build large-scale training and inference systems. Design and implement distributed training and RL post-training pipelines using frameworks such as PyTorch FSDP2, Megatron-LM, Miles, and verl. Build RL interaction harnesses using NeMo Gym or OpenEnv to connect agent workflows, tools, environments, and reward functions to training. Develop production inference stacks with engines such as SGLang and vLLM, and optimize throughput, latency, memory footprint, and cost per token through quantization, parallelism, speculative decoding, and batching.
  
  
Optimize models on AWS chips. Migrate and tune training and inference workloads for AWS Trainium using the AWS Neuron SDK. Profile performance, close accuracy-parity gaps against GPU baselines, and develop custom kernels where needed. Benchmark rigorously and turn results into decisions customers can act on.
  
  
Accelerate impact beyond the engagement. Codify reusable fine-tuning recipes, evaluation frameworks, benchmarking tools, and optimization patterns that accelerate future deployments. Feed field learnings back to AWS service teams, including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, and AWS Neuron. Identify opportunities to expand model customization and optimization within your customer engagement.

**About The Company**
CrowdStrike is a global cybersecurity company focused on stopping breaches and protecting the people, processes, and technologies that power modern organizations. Since 2011, the company has pursued this mission through its AI-native security platform, serving customers across a wide range of industries. CrowdStrike operates large-scale distributed systems that process nearly three trillion events each day, with that volume continuing to grow.
  
  
At CrowdStrike, innovation is connected to customer impact. Teams are encouraged to approach their work with curiosity, accountability, and a commitment to responsible AI adoption. Employees, known as CrowdStrikers, are empowered to bring new ideas forward, experiment thoughtfully, and work together to solve challenging problems.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Senior Software Engineer on the Infrastructure team, you will help develop and evolve the engineering tools and services that support CrowdStrike’s global systems. Your work will contribute to how teams build, deploy, and observe software, helping engineers deliver reliable capabilities as the platform and its customers grow. You will partner with colleagues across engineering to understand infrastructure needs, design practical solutions, and improve the systems that support development and operations.
  
  
This position calls for a hands-on engineer who can move between technical design and implementation, communicate clearly, and take ownership of complex work. You will contribute your judgment and experience while helping foster a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and responsible use of AI-enabled tools.
  
  
**Qualifications**
You bring substantial professional experience in software engineering and a track record of designing, implementing, and supporting production software. You have experience working with distributed systems or infrastructure-focused products and understand the importance of reliability, scalability, maintainability, and operational visibility. You are comfortable navigating complex technical environments and can evaluate trade-offs when choosing an approach.
  
  
You can communicate technical ideas clearly, collaborate across teams, and work effectively through ambiguity. You take responsibility for the quality and impact of your work, welcome feedback, and are interested in learning new tools and approaches. A thoughtful, security-conscious mindset and an interest in applying AI responsibly to improve engineering work are valuable in this role.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Design, build, test, and maintain software and infrastructure tools that enable engineering teams to develop, deploy, and observe services. Contribute to technical planning and system design, considering reliability, scale, operational needs, and maintainability. Investigate complex issues, identify root causes, and implement improvements that strengthen the infrastructure experience for users.
  
  
Work with engineering partners to understand requirements, align on solutions, and deliver improvements through the software lifecycle. Review code and designs, share knowledge, and help establish practices that support high-quality engineering. Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, improve observability, and reduce operational friction. Use AI-enabled tools responsibly where they can help accelerate execution, uncover insights, or support better problem-solving.
  
  
**Benefits**
Join a mission-driven organization working on consequential cybersecurity challenges and technologies used by customers across industries. CrowdStrike offers an environment that values flexibility, autonomy, innovation, and professional growth. ****Help build the next category-defining AI company****
AI has transformed how we write, communicate, and build software. The next frontier is even bigger: transforming how businesses actually operate. That's what we're building at Sola.
  
  
Sola is an AI-native platform reinventing enterprise process automation and disrupting legacy RPA tools. Our AI agents can execute complex workflows across any application, browser, desktop, or legacy system—free from the limitations and fragility of traditional automation tools. Users simply record their screen, and Sola creates a custom agent to run that process at scale.
  
  
The opportunity at hand is enormous. Nearly every enterprise, across every industry, runs on processes that are still painfully manual. We're building the technology to change that. And we're just getting started.
  
  
We're hiring a small group of
**Forward Deployed Engineers**
to help bring Sola to the world's largest enterprises and rewrite the playbook for how automation is built in the enterprise.
  
  
****Why Sola? Why now?****
**A massive market ready for reinvention.**
Enterprise automation is one of the biggest opportunities in AI. Legacy automation platforms have been constrained by rigid rules, complex implementations, and brittle workflows.. Sola is changing that with AI agents that can reason, adapt, and execute work across enterprise systems: the next generation of a massive software category.
  
  
**Real traction. Serious momentum.**
Sola today powers enterprise workflows across healthcare, finance, legal, logistics, and more, including at Fortune 500 companies. We've closed seven-figure enterprise deals with a lean team. The product is proven. The market is responding. Now we're building the team to scale it.
  
  
**Build Alongside Leaders Who've Done It Before.**
Work alongside David Fullerton, formerly CTO of Heap (Series C to acquisition) and Stack Overflow (Series A to E), as well as Sola's founders Neil Deshmukh and Jessica Wu. You'll have the opportunity to learn from exceptional engineers and help shape how the company grows.
  
  
**Early-stage ownership. Exceptional upside.**
Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Conviction, and Y Combinator, Sola has raised more than $20M to build the future of enterprise automation.
  
  
We’re still early enough that individual contributions can meaningfully influence the company’s trajectory, and you’ll have a direct influence on how the FDE role evolves over time.
  
  
****What you'll do****
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Sola, you'll combine hands-on technical execution with customer-facing communication and partnership.
  
  

* Dive deep on customer workflow failures using logs, browser tools, APIs, and code, then implement and verify fixes
* Build custom integrations and contribute production code to Sola's platform, turning recurring customer needs into reusable improvements
* Join customer calls alongside Customer Success, ask questions that clarify the problem, and own the solution through resolution
* Help customers onboard and adapt their workflows to Sola, including occasional travel for customer onboarding and key projects as needed

****Who we're looking for****
We're open to early-career engineers, new graduates with demonstrated programming ability, or strong customer-facing engineers who are comfortable writing production code.
  
  
You'll likely be a strong fit if you have:
  
  

* Strong technical foundations, whether from a CS degree with demonstrated coding abilities, or hands-on experience in a strong technical environment
* Flexibility to move across different customer environments, with a solid understanding of how core web technologies work and the ability to dive into complex desktop or legacy systems
* A strong sense of curiosity and a drive to go anywhere needed to solve tricky customer problems
* Excellent communication skills, and a demonstrated ability to turn complex technical findings into clear non-technical explanations

You'll work 5 days a week out of our office in NYC (we'll cover relocation!) and occasionally travel to customers as needed.
  
  
**Compensation & Benefits**
Sola offers competitive salary plus meaningful equity at Series A stage. Exact compensation is based on experience and level.
  
  
We offer comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits, 401(k) matching, daily meals together in the office, flexible PTO (4 weeks per year), and relocation support for candidates not already based in NYC.

**Description**
 AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations — from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3\) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2\), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS’s services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you’ll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (Iot), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS, including support for customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services.
   

  

 Do you want to work on a product that can do the following?:
   

  

 Access petabytes of data in single\-digit milliseconds
   

  

 Replicate tables across continents
   

  

 Stream terabytes of data updates per hour continuously
   

  

 Back up hundreds of terabytes of data in seconds
   

  

 Encrypt petabytes of data with no performance degradation
   

  

 Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database service that does all this and more. DynamoDB is a key\-value and document database that delivers single\-digit\-millisecond performance at any scale. DynamoDB can store petabytes of customer data and handle peaks of more than 20 million requests per second.
   

  

 As a fast growing service at the core of the AWS Cloud, our business and engineering decisions have widespread impact across AWS, Amazon, and beyond. Many of the world's fastest growing businesses, such as Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin, as well as enterprises, such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One, depend on the scale and performance of DynamoDB to support their mission\-critical workloads.
   

  

 DynamoDB is one of the largest distributed database systems in the world, and we continue to believe it is Day 1 for the DynamoDB business. We are constantly improving and adding new capabilities to DynamoDB, and we are looking for a deeply technical, team\-first software development engineer to push DynamoDB even further.
   

  

 DynamoDB engineers are constantly challenged to think of unique and innovative solutions. The quality bar is high. As an engineer here, you will work on the hardest engineering problems in distributed systems at a massive scale and on multiple dimensions. You will exercise your intellectual curiosity, work with motivated teams of sharp individuals, and get insightful guidance from senior and principal engineers.
   

  

 This is a hands\-on position in which you will own everything from end to end: requirements gathering, designs, design reviews, implementations, code reviews, incremental feature launches, operations, mentoring, and the driving of continuous improvement.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

 Design, build, and operate distributed infrastructure systems that provision, bootstrap, and manage the DynamoDB test cluster fleet. Specifically:
   

  

 Own systems end\-to\-end. Take a problem from design through implementation, deployment, and ongoing operation. No handoffs — you build it, you run it, you improve it based on production data.
   

  

 Deliver independently with minimal guidance. Break down ambiguous problems into executable plans. Your manager sets direction; you figure out the how and drive to completion.
   

  

 Debug complex distributed systems issues. Trace failures across multiple services, accounts, and regions. Identify root causes — not just symptoms — and fix them structurally.
   

  

 Write production\-quality code in Python and Java. Ship weekly. Maintain high standards for testing, monitoring, and operational readiness.
   

  

 Operate the fleet on\-call. Triage tickets, respond to alarms, and use what you learn operationally to drive reliability improvements back into the systems.
   

  

 Collaborate across teams. Engage partner teams to unblock dependencies, review designs, and align on technical approaches. Communicate clearly in writing and in person.
   

  

 Influence technical direction. Propose improvements, write design docs, and participate in architecture decisions. You're expected to have opinions backed by data and advocate for them.
   

  

 Mentor junior engineers and interns. Review code, give constructive feedback, and help others grow.
   

  

 In short: You will be a self\-sufficient engineer who can independently own a major workstream, operate what they build, and make the engineers around them more effective.
   

  

 A day in the life
   

  

 Your morning starts with a message: "My test environment won't come up." By 10am you've traced a deployment failure to a race condition between two services, shipped a fix, and unblocked a team of engineers whose pipeline is green again.
   

  

 By noon, you're designing automation that lets any engineer spin up a fully functional multi\-region DynamoDB test environment with a single command — replacing what used to take a week of manual configuration. You're thinking about cross\-region networking, security boundaries, and making complex infrastructure invisible to its users.
   

  

 After lunch, you're debugging a circular dependency that's been silently generating tickets for months. You find it, fix it, and close an entire class of failures.
   

  

 What makes this role different: You're building the infrastructure that lets every DynamoDB team validate their features before they ship to customers. When you make test environments faster and more reliable, you multiply the velocity of hundreds of engineers.
   

  

 The problems are deeply technical — distributed systems orchestration, fleet management, cross\-account security, credential rotation at scale — but you'll ship code every week and see immediate impact.
   

  

 The team is small (6 engineers), the scope is large, and the ownership is real. You'll design, build, and operate entire systems end\-to\-end. You'll work with Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, CloudFormation, EC2 fleet management, IAM, Python, and Java. You'll use AI coding tools daily.
   

  

 Every major DynamoDB launch validates on infrastructure your team builds. You make that possible.

The Air Dominance and Strike Low Observables Team are advancing into the next generation of LO Technology to enhance the survivability and effectiveness of unmanned air systems. **About The Role**
This is an early career role open to engineers with a degree in aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Low Observables work sits at the intersection of all three: the shape of the air vehicle, the electromagnetic behavior of its surfaces, and the materials and processes used to build it.
  
  
You do not need prior stealth experience. Almost nobody arrives with it, because most of it cannot be taught outside a cleared program. We will teach you the LO-specific methods. What we are looking for is strong engineering fundamentals, comfort picking up unfamiliar analysis tools, and the judgment to tell a real result from a bad one.
  
  
You will be paired with an LO engineer and start on a scoped piece of a live program, not a training exercise.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Run broadband Radar Cross Section (RCS) analysis on components and full air vehicles, and learn to judge when a prediction can be trusted
* Support the design and development of Low Observable unmanned air systems, from early configuration trades through detailed design
* Build and improve the analysis tools, scripts, and validation workflows the team runs on
* Model LO materials and treatments, and help select and optimize them for specific components
* Support manufacturing and validation planning, including tolerances, inspection methods, and what is actually producible at rate
* Help plan and execute RCS measurement campaigns in indoor chambers and on outdoor ranges, then reduce and interpret the data
* Compare measured results against predictions, chase down the disagreements, and feed what you learn back into the models

**Description**
The Amazon Search Navigation AI team helps customers go from a broad search intent to the few products that fit their needs, so they can make a confident purchase decision. We generate highly relevant, context-aware, and personalized search refinements. We also decide the order they appear in across Amazon's Search Navigation experiences, guiding customers to the most relevant results. The team owns Search Navigation's P0 metrics and defect guardrails, which keep performance and reliability high for hundreds of millions of customers.
  
  
We are reinventing search refinement with generative AI. Our recently launched Smart Refinement experience uses large language models (LLMs) served online to turn product specifications into natural-language suggestions that match how customers think, such as "for colder weather" or "lightweight for travel." Each suggestion is personalized to the customer's context. Next, we are building multi-turn, conversational refinement, where each interaction builds on the last and helps customers narrow their intent in fewer steps.
  
  
We build and run the engineering systems behind this work, including the Navigation Experience Service (NES). NES connects to Amazon's core search systems, serves more than 3 billion queries worldwide every day, and runs real-time LLM inference at global scale under strict latency and cost limits. Our platform supports launches of new navigation content and UIs, and it makes fast offline and online experimentation possible.
  
  
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer who is a pragmatic problem solver, comfortable with ambiguity, and curious about applied science. You will build and improve the Search Navigation platform, including the systems that serve LLMs in real time, and work closely with Applied Scientists to take new models from research into production.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Design, build, and operate large-scale, distributed, low-latency services that power Amazon Search Navigation experiences worldwide
* Build and optimize online LLM serving for Smart Refinement and multi-turn conversational refinement, with a focus on latency, reliability, and cost
* Work with Applied Scientists, Product Managers, and Program Managers to define requirements and integrate models into production systems
* Build scalable data pipelines that process large volumes of search and behavioral data for feature generation, model training, and evaluation
* Design, run, and analyze online A/B experiments to measure the impact of new models and features
* Contribute to operational excellence for critical services, including monitoring, on-call, and P0 metrics and defect guardrails
* Write high-quality, well-tested code and take part in design and code reviews

**Basic Qualifications**

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* 3+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
* 3+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
* 3+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
* 3+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
* Experience in developing and deploying LLMs in production on GPUs, Neuron, TPU or other AI acceleration hardware
* Experience in machine learning, data mining, information retrieval, statistics or natural language processing
* Experience with Machine Learning and Large Language Model fundamentals, including architecture, training/inference lifecycles, and optimization of model execution

**About the Role**

Jeeves is looking for an AI Engineer to help integrate artificial intelligence into its financial platform. The team is developing AI-powered capabilities for tasks such as intelligent spend categorization, anomaly detection, and large language model (LLM)-powered workflows that help finance teams work more efficiently.

This is an engineering-focused role centered on building and deploying AI systems for real-world financial applications, rather than conducting research. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists, and product teams to move AI solutions from prototypes into production.

The role requires a strong focus on reliability, observability, cost efficiency, and practical business value. You will also contribute to how Jeeves develops and scales its AI capabilities, with particular attention to the consequences of incorrect AI outputs when processing financial data.

**Key Responsibilities**

● Build and deploy AI-powered features for Jeeves' financial platform.

● Develop AI systems that support intelligent spend categorization, anomaly detection, and finance-related workflows.

● Build and maintain large language model pipelines for production use.

● Design and implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architectures.

● Move AI solutions from prototype to production in collaboration with backend engineering, data science, and product teams.

● Develop reliable, observable, and cost-efficient AI systems that deliver practical value to business customers.

● Operate and maintain machine learning systems in production.

● Address the challenges associated with AI errors and incorrect outputs in financial applications.

● Contribute to the development of AI engineering practices as the company expands its use of artificial intelligence.

**Required Experience and Technical Focus**

● Experience building LLM pipelines.

● Experience designing RAG architectures.

● Experience operating machine learning systems in production.

● A strong focus on building AI systems that are reliable, observable, and cost-efficient.

● An understanding of the challenges of deploying AI in financial contexts, where incorrect outputs can have real business consequences.

● Ability to work collaboratively with backend engineers, data scientists, and product teams to deliver production-ready AI features.

**Work Arrangement**

This is a full-time remote position.

**The Jeeves Approach**

Jeeves looks for people who demonstrate persistence and can make progress on difficult problems, including those without established solutions. The company emphasizes a steep learning curve, practical execution, and building technology that changes how money moves across borders.

As an AI Engineer, you will have the opportunity to help shape the use of AI across a growing financial platform and build systems that process real financial data for businesses.

**About The Company**
Capital One is using technology, data, and artificial intelligence to change banking for good. With a long history of applying machine learning to real-time, personalized customer experiences, the company continues to invest in advanced infrastructure and exceptional technical talent. Its AI capabilities help customers and associates with experiences ranging from identifying unusual transactions to getting answers in real time. Capital One is committed to developing responsible, reliable, and scalable AI systems that make banking simpler and more human.
  
  
The Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team works with partners across Capital One to advance AI science and engineering. The team develops and deploys proprietary models and platforms that enable business teams to build valuable AI-powered products for millions of customers and associates.
  
  
**About The Role**
Capital One is seeking an AI Engineer 4 to help build and advance foundational AI systems, with a focus on AI foundations and vision-language model (VLM) customization. You will partner with engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to create AI-powered products and production platforms. The role combines hands-on engineering with technical leadership, translating research into dependable systems that meet business needs.
  
  
You will contribute to the architecture and technical direction of complex AI systems, balancing performance, scalability, cost, latency, throughput, and accuracy. You will work with technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Hugging Face, vector databases, and PyTorch, while helping ensure that deployed solutions are observable, maintainable, secure, responsible, and aligned with applicable governance requirements.
  
  
**Qualifications**
Basic qualifications include a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field and at least four years of experience developing AI or machine learning algorithms or technologies; or a relevant master’s degree and at least two years of that experience. Applicants must also have at least four years of programming experience with Python, Go, Scala, CUDA, or Java.
  
  
Preferred qualifications include experience leading AI system development and making trade-offs among cost, latency, throughput, and accuracy; deploying scalable AI solutions on cloud platforms; and designing, delivering, and supporting AI services. Experience with model inference, similarity search, vector databases, guardrails, memory, agentic workflows, and training or inference optimization is valued. Familiarity with distributed systems, large-scale model evaluation, AI governance, lineage tracking, and automated retraining is also beneficial. Successful candidates bring strong engineering and mathematical foundations, curiosity about current research, sound judgment in applying new techniques, and the ability to communicate clearly and influence architectural decisions.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI components, including foundation-model training, large language model inference, agents and multi-agent workflows, similarity search, guardrails, evaluation, experimentation, governance, and observability. Develop optimization approaches that improve the performance and efficiency of production AI systems. Own architecture for complex solutions and contribute to the long-term roadmap for foundational AI at Capital One.
  
  
Define and maintain service-level objectives for reliability, including latency, uptime, and model performance drift. Partner with infrastructure engineering to improve GPU and TPU utilization and accelerate inference pipelines. Lead technical reviews for AI deployments, addressing security, data governance, and compliance. Collaborate across disciplines, investigate complex problems, share emerging ideas, and mentor colleagues in scalable design, performance tuning, and moving research into production.
  
  
**Benefits**
This role is eligible for performance-based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonuses and/or long-term incentives, subject to the applicable plan. Capital One provides a comprehensive benefits program supporting health, financial security, and overall well-being. Eligibility depends on factors including employment status and management level. The posted annual salary ranges are $197,300–$225,100 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and McLean, Virginia, and $215,200–$245,600 in New York, New York, and San Jose, California. Compensation for other locations may differ; the actual salary offer will be stated in the offer letter. Capital One will consider sponsorship for qualified applicants requiring employment authorization.

**Description**
As a Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) on the Custom Model and Optimization team, you embed directly with strategic customers to build, optimize, and run custom generative AI models in production alongside their engineering teams. You own complete model workstreams end-to-end from defining the evaluation bar and preparing data, through training and inference optimization, to production deployment.
  
  
FDE IIs on this team works at the intersection of models and systems. They customize state-of-the-art open-weight and foundation models for new domains, languages, and modalities; migrate and optimize training and inference workloads on AWS Trainium and operate those models as production services. They are autonomous contributors who take on projects where the business goal is clear, but the path is not. They make design trade-offs with appropriate guidance, limit short-term workarounds, coach others on producing high-quality code, and train new team members.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
Embed within customer ML and engineering teams: Understand the customer's business, data, model stack, and operational constraints. Translate ambiguous goals into a measurable evaluation bar and a technical plan for your workstream such as model selection, customization approach, and serving architecture. Requires up to 25% travel.
  
  
Customize and post-train models. Adapt open-weight and foundation models to customer domains through continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning (including RLHF, RL with verifiable rewards, and multi-turn agentic RL). Build the data pipelines, synthetic data generation, and evaluation harnesses that prove a customized model out performs the baseline on the customer's own quality, latency, and cost bar. Apply these techniques to high-value patterns such as coding agents, domain foundation models, and multi-adapter serving.
  
  
Build large-scale training and inference systems. Design and implement distributed training and RL post-training pipelines using frameworks such as PyTorch FSDP2, Megatron-LM, Miles, and verl. Build RL interaction harnesses using NeMo Gym or OpenEnv to connect agent workflows, tools, environments, and reward functions to training. Develop production inference stacks with engines such as SGLang and vLLM, and optimize throughput, latency, memory footprint, and cost per token through quantization, parallelism, speculative decoding, and batching.
  
  
Optimize models on AWS chips. Migrate and tune training and inference workloads for AWS Trainium using the AWS Neuron SDK. Profile performance, close accuracy-parity gaps against GPU baselines, and develop custom kernels where needed. Benchmark rigorously and turn results into decisions customers can act on.
  
  
Accelerate impact beyond the engagement. Codify reusable fine-tuning recipes, evaluation frameworks, benchmarking tools, and optimization patterns that accelerate future deployments. Feed field learnings back to AWS service teams, including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, and AWS Neuron. Identify opportunities to expand model customization and optimization within your customer engagement.

**About The Company**
Acro Service Corp works with organizations to support their workforce and business needs. In this role, you will collaborate with business-unit leaders, subject-matter experts, and information technology teams to develop analytics capabilities that support digital plans and business strategies. Your work may inform decisions involving external risks and opportunities, financial planning, economic development, customer and stakeholder engagement, regulatory reporting, and community involvement. You will help create tools and insights for audiences that may include local, state, and federal officials, industrial customers, and other community and business stakeholders.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a data science professional, you will model complex business problems and uncover insights through data mining, statistical analysis, predictive modeling, and visualization. You will develop and refine analytics products, proof of concepts, and automated solutions that can be incorporated into business processes. This role calls for sound analytical judgment and the ability to explain technical findings in a clear, concise, and actionable way. You will work with structured and unstructured data, explore emerging techniques in machine learning, deep learning, and artificial intelligence, and help colleagues use data more effectively in their decision-making.
  
  
**Qualifications**
A degree in mathematics, statistics, computer science, economics, engineering, operations research, decision science, or a related quantitative discipline is required, along with professional experience in analytics, statistical analysis, mathematical modeling, and computer programming. A master’s or doctoral degree is highly preferred. Candidates should have at least five years of experience with advanced analytics in an academic or professional setting; ten or more years is highly preferred. Relevant expertise may include predictive analytics, machine learning, deep learning, mathematical optimization, and risk simulation.
  
  
You should be comfortable working with large, varied datasets and applying appropriate analytical methods to business questions. The role also requires strong data visualization and presentation skills, the ability to communicate complex methods and results to different audiences, and a collaborative approach to working with business and technical teams. Experience with big data tools, automated analytics, or anomaly detection is valuable.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Identify business insights and opportunities using data structures, mining techniques, statistical methods, and predictive models. Gather, process, cleanse, and verify data; improve collection procedures; and incorporate relevant third-party information when appropriate. Analyze structured and unstructured sources, test for relationships and patterns, and select features and optimize classifiers using suitable machine-learning techniques. Define requirements for training and evolving deep-learning models and algorithms.
  
  
Design, test, and deliver reporting, visualization, and analytics products that support operational and executive decisions. Conduct ad hoc analyses and present findings clearly. Develop automated anomaly-detection systems and monitor their performance.
